problem: Prior typographic-attack work targets static 2D image classification or high-level navigation/driving decisions; the effect on the full Sense-Plan-Act pipeline of household robot manipulation (grasping the wrong object) has not been examined.
motivation: In modular manipulation stacks a perception error is written into a persistent 3D semantic map and propagates through all downstream planning to a physical grasp and delivery of the wrong object. CLIP/SigLIP-style joint embeddings used by open-vocabulary agents are structurally vulnerable to printed text, so this could be a real safety risk.
key_idea: Insert a frozen CLIP goal-scoring override on top of DETIC in the HomeRobot pipeline and place goal-name stickers in the scene to show that a single typographic misclassification poisons the voxel map and yields kinetic wrong-object pick-and-place.
insight: A single poisoned write to the persistent voxel map suffices: in all successful attacks the agent picked based on cached map coordinates without re-verification, and 37/40 picks were the sticker itself. The 19 failures were episodes where the sticker never pushed CLIP's score above the 0.28 threshold (attributed to viewing angle, occlusion and crop visibility). The threshold analysis argues that a hardening-by-threshold defense is not viable because goal and sticker scores overlap. Note the vulnerability is by construction, since the CLIP override was added by the authors, and there is no defense experiment.
method: Decoupled OvmmPerception: DETIC is kept only for proposals, masks and depth geometry, while a frozen CLIP scores each instance crop against 'a photo of a {goal}'.
Threshold-gated override: if the CLIP cosine similarity exceeds θ=0.28 (chosen from observed score ranges: non-goal 0.17-0.25, goal 0.28-0.30), CLIP replaces DETIC's semantic label.
3D semantic voxel map (5 cm): relabeled masks are backprojected into persistent memory, so a poisoned label persists after the sticker leaves view (cache-poisoning framing).
Heuristic FSM + FMM: Navigate-to-Object, Pick, Navigate-to-Receptacle, Place; snap-based manipulation in Habitat.
Attack configuration: one sticker bearing the goal name, placed on a flat surface closer to the agent's start than the true goal, with no perceptual optimization.
Episode attributability filter: only the 59 of 1,199 val episodes where the unattacked agent succeeds fully (10) or fails only at Place (49) are used.
Proposed mitigations (not evaluated): multi-view voxel confirmation, OCR-based anomaly detection, grasp-time re-query.

setting.backbone: HomeRobot pretrained agent with DETIC (detection/masks) + frozen CLIP (goal classification override)
setting.training_data: none (attack evaluation on pretrained/frozen components; no training)
setting.action_space: discrete Move/Turn navigation via FMM plus snap-based Pick/Place API calls
setting.privileged: Sticker placement chosen by the adversary using knowledge of the scene and the agent's expected path; attributable episodes selected using unattacked-agent outcomes.

numbers.eval_set_note: 59 attributable episodes out of 1,199 (10 fully successful + 49 failing only at Place)
numbers.method: Typographic sticker attack (CLIP override on HomeRobot), combined
numbers.extra: Attack success rate; ASR is the fraction of episodes where the agent picks a non-goal object; 40/59

numbers.method: Typographic sticker attack, fully successful episodes

numbers.eval_set_note: 49 episodes failing only at Place without attack
numbers.method: Typographic sticker attack, partially successful episodes

numbers_note: Only attack success rates are reported; no task SR/SPL baselines. Pre-attack failure distribution over 1,199 episodes is in a figure: ObjNav 860, Pick 159, Recep Nav 121, Place 49, Full success 10.
results: The sticker attack achieves 67.8% ASR (40/59) on the attributable pool, 70.0% on fully successful and 67.3% on partial episodes. 37/40 successes pick the sticker directly and 3/40 the foreground knife occluding it, and all 40 end at the Place phase with the wrong object transported or delivered.
limitations: The CLIP override is added by the authors; the unmodified HomeRobot (DETIC only) is not vulnerable, so the results depend on a proxy architecture.
Tiny, filtered evaluation pool (59 of 1,199 episodes) in simulation only, with a single sticker placed for maximum visibility and no defense or baseline comparisons; the mitigations are unevaluated.
